role_agent_name: Inert Gas and Suppression Systems Lead (GAS)
abstract: Maintains inert gas blanketing configuration, reserve storage autonomy, and purge rate records
system_message:
You are the Inert Gas and Suppression Systems Lead (GAS). Your business responsibility is to maintain official records on inert gas blanketing configuration, reserve storage autonomy, purge rates, and sensor calibration audits across archival vault facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Gas sensor calibration audit（CALIB）
information_points.content:
GAS-CALIB-NI4：At Eindhoven Fortified Lithography Depository, the scheduled sensor calibration cycle for certified recalibration of the vault oxygen depletion monitoring heads is 60 days.
GAS-CALIB-9B5：For Grenoble Alpine Subsurface Chamber, certified maintenance records document a sensor calibration cycle of 90 days across the vault oxygen depletion monitoring heads.
GAS-CALIB-3FS：Calibration maintenance logs for Dresden Bedrock Reticle Sanctum show a scheduled sensor calibration cycle of 30 days for the vault oxygen depletion monitoring heads.

information_points.title: Maintains inert gas blanketing configuration, reserve storage autonomy, and purge rate records（INERT）
information_points.content:
GAS-INERT-XXA：At Grenoble Alpine Subsurface Chamber, continuous nitrogen blanketing is actively enabled for the archival reticle storage pod bays according to the atmospheric gas control console. The dedicated liquid nitrogen bulk tank sustains a nitrogen storage autonomy of 48 h of continuous operation without resupply, and manifold flow testing establishes a nitrogen blanket purge rate of 500 m3/h.
GAS-INERT-02S：Records for Eindhoven Fortified Lithography Depository indicate that continuous nitrogen blanketing is enabled across the archival reticle storage pod bays. The facility maintains a nitrogen storage autonomy of 72 h from its on-site cryogenic bulk tank, with emergency high-velocity nozzles delivering a nitrogen blanket purge rate of 600 m3/h.
GAS-INERT-L2F：For Dresden Bedrock Reticle Sanctum, the atmospheric gas control console confirms that continuous nitrogen blanketing is enabled in the archival reticle storage pod bays. The on-site cryogenic bulk storage tank provides a nitrogen storage autonomy of 72 h without external resupply, and gas delivery manifold flow testing verifies a nitrogen blanket purge rate of 500 m3/h through the high-velocity emergency inerting nozzles.
